verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

notes: history.csv / sheet 'history' is a single flat price-history export: 24 rows, 12 SKUs x 2 validity periods (2026-10-01 and 2026-11-01), each period carrying one active and one expired row. Role classified as pricing; a products-level record must be assembled by grouping on SKU.

Operator requirement: export active prices only — rows with 'Record state' = expired must be filtered out, and the surviving row's 'Valid from' must be retained as /prices/*/effective_from. Because no 'Valid to' column exists, /prices/*/effective_to stays null; the end of the expired interval is not available evidence and is not synthesised.

Leading zeros: the SKU column was profiled as integer (min 470001, max 470012) although its cells display as 00470001…00470012. The mapping must cast/zero-pad to the original 8-character string form (e.g. 00470001) before it becomes /sku; identifiers are kept as text.

Business facts carried from the file, not inferred: currency THB (constant), sales unit PCS (constant), price_list 'standard' (constant + operator confirmation), tax included = No on every row, tax rate 5% on every row. The 5% is a fictional fixture value written in the source, not an assumption and not the schema's 0.07 default; no rate conversion is applied beyond percent→fraction.

No VAT adjustment is needed: Tax included = No already states the vat_included = false semantics explicitly, so vat_adjust must not be applied and net prices are passed through unchanged (no amount is back-computed).No FX conversion, per operator instruction (single currency anyway).No brand, category, barcode, description, pack size, warehouse/stock, promotion or reserved-quantity columns exist in this file, so those optional pointers receive no values; pack_size, /category, /barcode, /brand, /description, /inventory and /promotions stay absent/null rather than guessed.

No actionable business questions remain for this table: every column's meaning is settled by its header, its constant or per-row values, the target-field synonyms, or the operator's explicit instructions.

tables.reason: Each of the 24 rows pairs a SKU/product name with a currency, sales unit, a single named price list ('standard'), a net price, a VAT flag, a VAT rate and a validity start date — a price-list export per material with time-sliced validity. Two rows per SKU (12 distinct SKUs x 2) correspond to the two 'Valid from' dates (2026-10-01 / 2026-11-01) and the two 'Record state' values (active/expired), i.e. a product price history keyed by SKU with price validity intervals. No stock, no promotion or category data present.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU' matches the sku synonym list; 12 distinct values, 2 rows each. Values were read as numbers (470001) although they display with leading zeros (00470001) — must be cast back to a zero-padded 8-character string per operator instruction to preserve leading zeros.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name' is an exact product_name synonym; distinct values one per SKU, e.g. 'SIM replenishment 1'.

columns.name: Currency
columns.reason: Header 'Currency' is an explicit currency synonym; single value 'THB' on all 24 rows, an ISO-4217 code matching the ^[A-Z]{3}$ pattern. No FX conversion needed.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header 'Sales unit' is a unit.sell synonym; single constant value 'PCS', which normalises to the canonical enum value PCS via unit_normalize. No pack size is stated anywhere, so /unit/pack_size stays null.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list' is a direct price.list_name synonym; single value 'standard', which the operator requirement explicitly confirms as the price_list value and which coincides with the schema default.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price' is a price.amount synonym ('net price'); one distinct numeric value per row, range 1134.56–1356.77, never empty — a unit selling price. Column holds no currency symbol, so it is not parsed from mixed text.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header 'Tax included' is an explicit vat_included synonym; the only value is 'No' on all 24 rows, so vat_included = false via parse_bool. The paired explicit 'Tax rate' column corroborates that VAT is stated separately rather than being implied.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate' plus a uniform value of '5%' — an explicit source tax rate, converted to the schema's fraction form 0.05 with parse_number_th(percent_to_fraction). This is a fixture rate from the file, not a default; the schema default 0.07 is not applied.

columns.name: Valid from
columns.reason: Header 'Valid from' is an effective_from synonym and values are ISO dates (2026-10-01, 2026-11-01) with no day/month ambiguity, so no date_format question is needed. The operator requirement fixes the interval start on the surviving active record. No matching 'Valid to' column exists in the source, so /prices/*/effective_to is left null rather than derived.

columns.name: Record state
columns.reason: Header 'Record state' with values 'expired' (12) and 'active' (12), exactly splitting the two date intervals; it marks whether a price row is the current or the superseded one, and the operator requirement says to keep active rows only and drop expired ones. It is a row-level selection flag for /prices, not a product lifecycle status: 'expired' is not in the /status enum (active/inactive/discontinued) and a whole product is not discontinued merely because an older price interval ended, so it is deliberately not mapped to /status.

changes_from_draft: Added a record filter on 'Record state' = active so expired price rows are excluded and one product is emitted per SKU (12 active rows → 12 products), per the operator requirement to export active prices only.
Added the same filter on the /prices collection so only the active price row becomes a price item; the expired interval is dropped rather than merged.
SKU now cast to string (trim + cast to string) to preserve the zero-padded 8-character form 00470001..00470012; the previous trim-only expression risked a numeric rendering.
Added /prices/*/effective_from from 'Valid from' (parse_date_th, ISO y-m-d, CE) — the operator asked to retain effective_from for the active record.
Added /prices/*/vat_rate from 'Tax rate' 5% → 0.05 (explicit source value, overriding the schema default 0.07); 'Tax rate' was previously listed as an unmapped column.
vat_included now derives from the source flag via parse_bool('Tax included' = 'No' → false) with default false, instead of a bare const.
price_list now read from the 'Price list' source column ('standard') with trim, instead of a const; the value is explicit in the data.

Removed the /status mapping: 'Record state' is a price-row validity flag (active/expired) and 'expired' is not in the /status enum; product status stays unmapped and the schema default 'active' applies. 'Record state' is kept on /attributes by passthrough.
Added record-level dedupe on /sku and collection dedupe on /price_list + /effective_from (the schema identity keys).
/prices/*/effective_to left unmapped: the file has no 'Valid to' column and no end date is synthesised.
/unit/pack_size, /brand, /category, /barcode, /description, /inventory and /promotions receive no values — no source columns carry that evidence; nothing is invented.
Currency THB and unit PCS are constant source values, not inferences from brand or country; no FX conversion applied.
